newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar erases gains but trade supportive.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar erases gains but trade supportive.

text.p: London's August white sugar contract on Wednesday eroded this month's gains after it gapped lower at the open and then hit concerted selling from commission houses and European brokers.

August weakened on Tuesday as one French brokerage sold the outright position and the August/October spread. Other players took profits as the market fell and took the opportunity to roll spot positions into October.
August then fell further in early Wednesday trading led by commission house and more broker sales, along with pre-hedging against the European Union's weekly tender for sugar export licences.
"August doesn't look that great at all...it looks like some pre-hedging came in early this morning and sparked some people going again," said one trader.
August opened 80 cents lower on Wednesday at $324.20, still 30 cents below Tuesday's intraday low.
But trade buying was supportive on the dips, dragging August off its low of $321.50.
"There seems to some fair support, once you get a dollar lower a few of the trade start to look at pricing in that sort of areas," the trader said.
At 1135 GMT August was $2.60 lower at $322.40 and October down $1.00 at $315.70. Volume was concentrated in August and amounted to an overall 1,344 lots.
Traders said August/October also commanded reasonable interest and narrowed to $6.50/7.00 from around $8.00/8.50 on Tuesday.
Last week's fund-inspired rally which pushed August to a high of $330.80 was overdone and so the market naturally looked for a downward correction, they said.
Nearby positions also weakened in Paris where volume totalled 188 lots. August was down $2.20 at $321.80 and October untraded.
Fundamentally, traders said results have yet to emerge in Iran's tender to buy 30,000 tonnes of raw sugar for June/July shipment.
